# Gameplay Coverage

Every retained feature traced from where the player meets it to what it changes and who reads the change: entry, preconditions and state read, the calculation and the state changed, the downstream consumer, what persists, how it is explained, and what tests it. Audited on 2026-10-10 against `43d10f8b`, and its open items revisited after `9ae9879b` (`docs/verification/open-items.json` holds each one’s disposition, recorded before the work, and its outcome). Written by `node tools/coverage.mjs` from `docs/verification/audit/*.json`.

Audited again on 2026-10-12, after the connected-journey pass, and every row that pass changed was brought up to date (Corrected On 2026-10-12, below). Four reviews of that audit the same day found it said more than was done, and every row they named was settled by the standard below; the rows read by eye against it are listed under Read By Eye, and the Totals count the verified rows read apart from those called verified and not read. The third found 36 commands that came in after the audit and its revisit (from `f899ecd7`, 2026-10-10, and later) in no row, while this page said every retained feature was traced; each is traced and read now (Traced On 2026-10-12, below). The fourth found rows verified on the change alone, or on a reader the clock calls run by the test in its place: a medical debt’s report a year on, a tax plan revised or caught up and never played on, a term’s maturity after its interest is taken, a stopped debit card’s purchases, a dismissed decision’s refusal, savings linked behind the current account and never reached by a card’s autopay or a loan, and an overdraft’s fee once opted into; each is partial now and says what isn’t checked. Checking what the fourth settled, the same day, found more verified on a reader no test reaches through the command: an elective shift’s payday and the wages it records for the return, a kept plan’s hold on sleep and Look After, a treatment’s later months, tolls and emergencies, what a doctor chosen decides, a meal’s hunger toll, and a decision acted on refused a second time; each is partial now too. Every row is checked by `tools/coverage.mjs`, which writes this page and fails when one doesn’t hold: each test it names by its title is in the file it names, each line it or its Note cites falls inside a test, every line of every range, a row called verified names a test in the gate, and a command called verified names a test file that issues it, its action too. It fails as well where this page and `docs/capabilities.json` disagree on a command: every command a live capability names is in a row here or in the connected-journey trace (158 are here); a capability called Verified has every row of its commands verified and read; a command not verified here isn’t under a capability whose verified layer says Verified, and the capability’s limits name each of its rows not verified, by the row’s own name (life.look_after:wash for one of its actions), in a sentence that gives its word here, partial, or unresolved (or out of reach) where only a fixture reaches it; and a command reached only by a fixture sits in a capability called Partial. Until the fourth review it held only the first, a Verified capability’s rows verified, and the last, so a capability called Implemented or Partial could be silent on a command this page calls partial, or keep Verified in its verified layer; and until its settlement was checked a sentence naming a command named every action of it, so limits that called one action of life.look_after partial passed for three more. Whether the rest of what the limits say of a command agrees with its row (that they don’t call checked what the row calls partial) is held by reading. Whether a test checks what reads the change is held only by reading: until the first review this page said every test a row names was read for it, until the second the rows read were named in a sentence somebody typed, and until the third the Totals counted every row called verified as verified, read or not. What the pass added is traced in `docs/verification/connected-journey/TRACE.md`: a piece judged in its segments, the scene together with a partner or a company, the workbook’s commands, a brief’s reader, the director’s craft notes, the actor’s work so far, and the guide’s reference. Until 2026-10-16 none of its commands was a row here; from then (brief 09) the brief’s, the workbook’s and the ways of playing are, with `life.look_after` as a command, each under Added Since The Review.

**Verified**: traced end to end, and a named test in the gate (`tests/*.test.ts`) checks what the row says reads the change (its Downstream), driving the change through the engine, by a command or the clock. A test that sets the change or its reader’s input by hand, or calls a function in place of the command or the clock, checks less: the row says so, and where what reads the change is checked only that way, or not at all, it’s partial. A reader the clock calls on its own (the day’s draw, the idle check, a rehearsal kept) called by the test in its place, or given its draw, is one of those. A precondition set by hand (wages typed in, a document put in) is setup, where the command and what reads it still run through the engine. A reader called after the command, on the state the command left, is checked by that call: its figure read (cardRoom after card.lock), or a purchase made through the engine’s own spend, the way every day’s shopping is made, where spend is what reads the change. What checks less is the same reader called on state set by hand, given its draw, or run in place of the clock that runs it: a function called in place of the command or the clock. Until the fourth review this page counted those two as setup without drawing that line, and `docs/capabilities.json` said any function called directly checked less, so a row could pass one standard and owe a word under the other. On a life no new one lives, the row says that too where the place decides what’s tested (a bank’s terms, a state’s or a country’s rule, a published wait). The rows the third review read say it; until then most bank rows ran on New York, Icelandic or London lives and didn’t. A reader that only shows (a suggestion, a look) is under Explained, not Downstream. A trait or a knob is the input itself, so its row is checked by twins: a test that varies it alone and checks the reader the row names. A Home or Profile row is a panel, and what it shows and what its controls do are what it’s for: it’s verified where a test renders it and checks that, the row naming what the test doesn’t read, and a test of the engine function a panel calls checks the figure, not the panel. `tools/acceptance-ui.mjs` plays the built app outside the gate: it can support a row and never makes one verified alone. Until 2026-10-12 a test that exercised the command was taken for that, and rows were verified on a test that checked the change and not its reader, on a fixture no new life reaches, or on no test; they’re corrected below. A row called verified and not read is verified only as the audit of 2026-10-10 and the open-items revisit left it: its Status says so, and the Totals don’t count it as verified. Mutation-tested only where a repair’s commit says so; the rest were traced, not mutated. **Partial**: works, with a named gap (untested, tested only by hand or as a function, or a consumer missing). **Unresolved**: declared or reachable only through systems the owner removed, or reached only by a fixture (a place no new life lives, such as a bank, a card or a country’s rule no New Haven life has), reported rather than deleted, each with its recommendation where the owner decides. **Legacy**: a compatibility path for a save from before 2026-10-09, tested through legacy state; no new life reaches it. **Informational**: said back to the player and meant to decide nothing (a name, a portrait).

## Totals, By How Each Row Is Evidenced

From 2026-10-16 each row carries an evidence class beside its status (`verification` in `docs/verification/audit/*.json`, written by the pipeline's `merge-review.cjs`), so the totals above can't hide how a row is verified or why it's out of reach. The class moves no status, and `tools/coverage.mjs` fails a row whose evidence doesn't bear its class out. **Player Journey**: a test in the gate reaches the action as a player does (a command, the clock or the rendered screen, not on a fixture), checks the consequence and expects independently; verified, or partial with its gap named. **Retained Engine, On Labelled Fixtures**: no current player reaches the action, and its engine is tested on lives or state labelled FIXTURE or TEST SETUP; unresolved, kept in the denominator, each saying in four parts what a Yale player meets, the engine's tests, whether the owner defers it and what's unfinished (below). **Documentation And Static Checks**: the row's claim is the repository's own text, tested against that text by a static test that meets the standard below. **Deferred Scope**: the owner's, out of this build. Two more fit none of those four, and are their status: **Older Saves Only**, a path only a save from before reaches, and **Said Back, Deciding Nothing**, a selection said back that decides nothing. Until 2026-10-16 a test titled FIXTURE was recorded by the kind its round named, a command or a render, in 51 tests of 22 rows; each is a fixture now, and no verified row rested on them alone.

The 16 deferred, 3 legacy and 8 informational rows are outside what can be verified, as the status totals have them.

### The Static Kind, From 2026-10-16

**static**: a test in the gate that reads the repository's own text (its code, tests or documents) and checks a claim about that text. It was added on 2026-10-16, when the owner's brief of that day answered yes the decision of 2026-10-15 (`docs/verification/CURRENT-SCOPE-2026-10-15.md`, The Owner's Decisions, 1): whether a row whose claim is the repository's own text can be verified by a gate test that reads that text. It applies only to such a row, and verifies one only where the test meets the same three tests a player journey's does, read and written into the row (`standard`): it reaches the text the claim is about (the files themselves, not a copy or a summary), checks it, and expects independently, with examples it must catch and examples it must accept, so that a check passing everything fails its first and one failing everything its second, and a walk that reads nothing fails its own count. Each example is quoted as it stands in the test's file, and `tools/coverage.mjs` fails a row whose example isn't there. A static test of any other row supports it and never verifies it. Until 2026-10-16 such a test was recorded as a fixture, and i-stale-claims stood partial on the player-action standard, its note of 2026-10-15 kept in the row (`verification.was`).

## The Review Of 2026-10-13

The owner’s brief of 2026-10-13 asked for every coverage claim held to one standard. Every row here and every live capability was read on that day against `fca00d8f` by readers who changed nothing: what the row claims, the code and what reads the change, each test’s assertions read, whether the test reaches the action as a player does and checks the consequence with an expectation of its own, and the UI evidence a row about a screen needs. Each row keeps it as `review` in `docs/verification/audit/*.json`. The evidence is recorded by kind: **command** (a test in the gate that issues the command or runs the clock), **render** (a test in the gate that renders the screen and reads it), **fixture** (state set by hand, or a function called in place of the command or the clock), **inspection** (the code read), **built-app** (`tools/acceptance-ui.mjs`, outside the gate) and **long-run** (played lives and scenarios). Only the first two make a row verified, and only where the test reaches the action, checks the consequence and expects what an independent reading of the rule gives; the rest support. From 2026-10-16 a seventh kind, **static** (a test in the gate that reads the repository’s own text), verifies a row whose claim is that text and no other, where it meets the standard under The Static Kind, From 2026-10-16. The pass that followed added 1562 tests in 91 files for the rows the review left partial, fixed 185 defects the tests found, and ran 1010 mutations of the code those tests protect, 1004 of them killed; what each row gained is its `after`.

## Corrected On 2026-10-12

160 rows were corrected when the matrix was audited again on 2026-10-12 and reviewed four times, 8 of them from verified: 1 to partial, and 7 to unresolved, reached only by a fixture. Each said more than its test checked, was verified on a fixture no new life reaches, named a test by a name it no longer has or none that checks it, described what the code no longer does, or didn’t say its tests ran on a life no new one lives where the place decides what they test. A row a review found moved the wrong way is back where its test puts it, and says so. A row says what it said and what it says now, with the evidence; the same words are in its Note below. Nothing here is new functionality: where the code changed, the row says when and why.

| Area | Item | Status | Said | Says Now |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Life, Health And Time | life.sleep | verified | Note: hours not validated as finite (the clamp passed NaN), and a start with no upper bound. Verified, while no cited test slept through a commitment. | From 2026-10-10 a night asks a number of hours and a start within the day ahead (tests/life-fixes.test.ts). Through the command, a night moves the clock by its hours, restores energy and pays down the debt, and is slept once whatever midnight it crosses (simulation.test.ts). No test sleeps through a commitment with life.sleep and checks what reads it: present() or the PLAN_KIND handler marking it missed, or the notice. The therapy session slept through (life-fixes.test.ts) sets awakeSince by hand, and plans.test.ts misses a plan through advanceTo. No inHospital check. |
| Life, Health And Time | life.look_after:eat | verified | Downstream: readiness, and applyElapsedWellbeing’s hungry hours on condition and morale; verified on tests that read readiness and the mood a meal lifts. | Through the command, a meal feeds and leaves readiness above the same afternoon without one (looking-after.test.ts:37-45), lifts a spender’s mood more than a frugal person’s (traits-connected.test.ts), and is paid from cash in hand where a locked debit card can’t pay (defects-g4-1.test.ts). From 2026-10-12 the menu and the command refuse it in the words of spendRefusal, spend’s own precondition, for every way of paying (defects-r1-1.test.ts), and it’s paid as it’s ordered, before its hour, so one whose hour crosses midnight is bought ahead of the day’s groceries rather than offered and then refused (defects-r3a-1.test.ts); until then the row read canPay, which counted cash in hand for every payer. The hunger toll a meal spares, applyElapsedWellbeing’s hungry hours on condition and morale, isn’t checked after one: it’s tested on applyElapsedWellbeing called on dials set by hand (personality.test.ts), and the half-year test that eats among four actions a day (wellbeing-bites.test.ts) can’t tell a meal’s part. Still open: partial: The plan's part of a bill is real and played. A played life with need reaches a program renewal by the clock alone (tests/need-paths.test.ts): she is withdrawn, enrolled in HUSKY D on Papers, and her renewal on 1 November 2027 passes the income test on interest alone, then fails Connecticut's 2027 work test, so HUSKY D ends and she's told. A renewal that keeps a program is reached too: an Inherited family's student enrolls in Covered Connecticut on a personal leave, on January's interest, and it renews on 1 September 2027 on August's interest, by play alone (tests/scope-cover.test.ts); need-paths plays HUSKY D moved to Covered Connecticut at renewal. Until the recheck of 2026-10-15 this said no renewal that keeps a program was reached and Covered Connecticut's couldn't be: that reckoning assumed a family with need and work-study income, and overlooked the interest an Inherited life earns. What stays open is HUSKY D kept at renewal through work: SLATE pays wages only for work-study and the Summer Cabaret, both a student's, so a life off Yale Health has none, and the tests give it as TEST SETUP wages. From the recheck, HUSKY D's work test reads the School over last month, as 42 CFR 435.552(c) has it, at an application and at a renewal; until then it read the School at the instant asked, and a student at the School all of January 2027, withdrawn on 1 February, was refused on 2 February. HUSKY D kept by her being at the School is played (tests/scope-cover.test.ts, back from a leave). No income was invented and no eligibility loosened. |

Downstream: purchaseMayOverdraw (lending.ts:317-323) is read by spend (spending.ts:320-386) and spendRefusal (:263-289); chargeForItem (lending.ts:526-573) holds the item, and settlePendingItems (:833-852) charges it after the next business day. Tests: also tests/evidence-g10-money.test.ts 'bank.debit_overdraft', with the clock's groceries at Chase (its $34 fee on 27 August) and at Wells Fargo, and the refusals at Citi, Capital One and Bank of America. |

The bank screen draws that panel for the primary account's bank only (BankWorkspace.tsx:200), so a deposit at a second bank is put away after making that bank's account primary, and the panel passes that bank's id. Changes: the command lending.ts:1330-1353, funded from the current account at that bank. Downstream: lending_day accrual and maturity at lending.ts:1059-1093 (endTerm accountlife.ts:430-457); the secured overdraft's room at lending.ts:385-386 in overdraftRoom (:372-387); break_term and set_term_end. accountlife.test.ts:210-224, 237-259 (Toronto and Berlin lives); defects3-bank.test.ts ‘LIFE FIXTURE (Toronto): a Citi loan repaid from TD, TD empty at the due date: TD’s $10 from TD, nothing from RBC, the primary’ (the returned fee taken where the loan is repaid, chargeReturned lending.ts:592; until 2026-10-13 it came from the primary); evidence-g11-money.test.ts ‘bank.set_payments > takes a Citi loan’s monthly payment from Chase Savings when it falls due, with the link pressed On, and misses it onto the record with the link Off’; evidence-g11-money.test.ts ‘bank.set_payments > puts the night’s groceries where The Day’s Spending, changed on How You Pay, says: on the credit card, then in cash, then on the debit card’; evidence-g11-money.test.ts ‘bank.set_payments > is refused On once Chase Savings is closed through Close Savings, in the bank’s words, isn’t drawn on How You Pay, and goes On once savings is opened there again’ | command 7, render 1, fixture 1; 8 hold; 3 from the rounds since 2026-10-13 | verified | partial | Through the command, the day’s shopping made through spend goes on the credit card, or comes out of the wallet first, as chosen (payments.test.ts:78-86, cash.test.ts:134-149), and savings linked pay what the current account can’t, and only where linked (payments.test.ts:51-67), on Icelandic lives; linked at RBC and Deutsche Bank, a bill paid from savings is charged its withdrawal fee and held to Germany’s allowance (accountlife.test.ts:210-224, 237-259). From 2026-10-12 the link draws, for every payment, on easy-access savings at the bank of the current account the payment comes from: the primary for the day’s spending, the account a card’s autopay is set on for that autopay, and a loan’s repayment account for the loan; a change of primary leaves a card’s autopay and a loan’s repayment where they were. How You Pay lists each paying account and what it pays, and turning the link On is refused only where none has such savings. With Chase savings, a Citi loan repaid from Chase and Citi made primary, the link is offered, turned On, and pays the loan off from Chase savings (bank.repay_loan), and a card’s autopay left on Chase is paid from Chase savings through the clock where until then it bounced (defects-r3b-1.test.ts). Until then this row read ‘savings existence’, and said the card’s autopay reaching linked savings wasn’t checked. What isn’t: a loan’s monthly payment drawn from them by the clock (lending.test.ts sets the link by hand and doesn’t check which account paid; defects-r3b-1.test.ts pays the loan off by the command). The fourth review didn’t name this row; it was read while settling the rows it did. |

Downstream: card.interest skips accrual on a plan (credit.ts:947). autopayAsk (credit.ts:1062-1070) makes the plan's payment both what autopay asks and what the due date judges. Met, the month counts on time (+3) and the missed count goes back to none (credit.ts:903-904). The plan ends once nothing is owed, at a due date (:918-921) or a statement (:795). cardRoom is 0 while suspended (credit.ts:556). The statement's notice asks the plan's payment (credit.ts:806), and so does the Statements page (BankStatements.tsx, onPlan). |

Until that day no life made at Yale banked in Germany and the row was unreachable, as it said; the account kept at home of that day made it reachable, which the coverage area’s probe found the same day. tests/integration-savings-notice.test.ts plays it from creation: a Berlin-raised student keeping Deutsche Bank presses Close It on the Bank screen on 1 September 2026 with €6,264.00 in her Flexgeld, past the €2,000 the month lets out; the notice is given, and on 1 December 2026 the clock closes the Flexgeld whole into her AktivKonto, its interest paid first, the $10 order into it ended, said once, across a reload, and the same in one jump as day by day; a scraping family’s €64.00 closes at once with no notice. Four mutations of the close, each in a copy, were killed. The money on its way to another bank, which only a switch leaves, is still held on FIXTURE lives living in Berlin; no current life reaches it. Read by the coverage area, which wrote the test, and checked by no separate skeptic. |

The coverage area’s probe found it (probe/coverage09/tax-lien.ts, its output in docs/verification/remaining-09/coverage-result.json), and tests/remaining-09-coverage.test.ts plays it: the substitute assessed 485 days after the 18 April 2028 due date, the LT11 140 days on files the notice of lien, the levy 30 days on pays it, it’s released 30 days after, Form 12277 is refused while 2028’s return is unfiled, in the engine’s words, and pressed on the lien panel once it’s filed, the lien withdrawn 30 days on, said once across a reload; the Wealthy family’s twin, its LT11 under $10,000, has no lien. Three mutations, each in a copy (the three years’ rule made false, the threshold at $15,000 and at $10), were killed. A lien filed in error stays reached only by a fixture: the IRS’s figures leave out only the foreign tax credit and the premium tax credit. Read by the coverage area, which wrote the test, and checked by no separate skeptic. |

The owner's scope of 2026-10-09 (bcc30c88) removed the home: person.home, with its rent and bills. With it went every way a player stood apart from where they live: jobs on location, sublets, relocation, and the Travel panel Home.tsx's header says went that day. Since then homeCityOf (src/engine/world/place.ts:102-105) returns CITIES.get(currentLocationId) first, and nothing writes currentLocationId after creation (bootstrap.ts:354, decided.ts:154 only). So placeProfile's `away` is always false for the city Home profiles. A currentLocationId moved by hand reads 'Home.' in the new city, so not even a fixture reaches it. The branch and the stale docstring are reported for removal under defects. |
